AuMgO / cumulene / bio_dimers: checkpoint-parity diagnostics from metawork-54¶

This notebook visualizes raw diagnostic data generated by a peer Claude session (metawork-54), working in lorem-tmlr-archive on the same torch-port-of-lorem-jax effort as this project's 15_long_range_scan_lorem_jax_ported_torch.ipynb (via JaxParityBackbone/JaxParityLongRange), on AuMgO (a periodic slab) and bio_dimers (periodic, large box) -- plus cumulene (a warm-started fine-tune, snapshotted mid-run).

Update: the periodic (AuMgO, bio_dimers) discrepancy described in sections 1-6 below has since been root-caused and fixed -- see section 7 onward and the updated Takeaways at the end. Sections 1-6 are kept as originally written, as the record of the investigation that found the bug; they no longer describe the current state of the code.

1. AuMgO: stage-by-stage parity (torch port vs jax reference)¶

For one AuMgO frame (110 atoms), metawork-54 captured the intermediate output of every module in the forward pass on both the jax reference (flax.linen's capture_intermediates=True) and the torch port, and recorded (torch_value, jax_value, diff) for each. Unlike this project's SN2 port (15_long_range_scan_lorem_jax_ported_torch.ipynb, agreement ~2e-5 eV), this AuMgO port is not yet fully closed -- the scalar-only stages (Dense_0, Update_0, Update_1, MLP_0, MLP_1) match near the float32 noise floor, but every tensor/spherical-valued stage (TensorDense_0, TensorDense_1, Dense_3, Tensor_0 -- orange bars) shows a large elementwise difference, consistent with an e3x component-ordering or CG-phase-convention mismatch (the same class of issue e3x_compat.py/test_e3x_parity.py exist to handle for the SR path, but evidently not fully resolved for every module here). Interestingly, the rotationally-invariant scalar quantities computed from those tensors (Update_1, Update_2) partially self-correct, and the final TOTAL per-atom energy differs by only ~0.06 eV -- much better than the raw tensor-stage differences suggest, but still not float32-noise-level like the SN2 case.

import pickle
import numpy as np

with open("metawork54_results/intermediate_diagnostics.pkl", "rb") as fh:

for stage, (torch_v, jax_v, diff) in diag.items():

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.patches import Patch

BLUE, ORANGE = "#0072B2", "#D55E00"
tensor_stages = {"TensorDense_0", "TensorDense_1", "Dense_3", "Tensor_0"}
stages = list(diag.keys())
max_diff = [float(np.abs(diag[s][2]).max()) for s in stages]
colors = [ORANGE if s in tensor_stages else BLUE for s in stages]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 5))
ax.bar(range(len(stages)), max_diff, color=colors)
ax.set_yscale("log")
ax.set_xticks(range(len(stages)))
ax.set_xticklabels(stages, rotation=40, ha="right", fontsize=8)

                   Patch(facecolor=ORANGE, label="tensor/spherical-valued stage")],
          fontsize=8, loc="upper left")

2. AuMgO: total-energy parity across 20 frames¶

Energies here are ~1.48 million eV (a full periodic slab total, not per-atom) -- so a 0.19 eV max discrepancy is a tiny relative error, but on an absolute scale it's far short of the SN2 port's ~2e-5 eV.

4. AuMgO: Ewald-potential channels¶

10 predicted-multipole potential channels (channel 0 = scalar charge potential; channels 1-9 = spherical, degrees l=0,1,2 flattened), torch-port vs jax.

Correction (per metawork-54's follow-up check, after I first flagged this panel as a possible dead-channel bug): the original index-by-index comparison was not a valid channel-to-channel match for most of the l>=1 slots -- lorem-jax's e3x builds spherical components in a different per-degree order than this torch port's own convention (a documented, benign permutation, metatrain.experimental.lorem.modules.e3x_compat._permutation_indices). metawork-54 supplied the correctly-permuted torch array (AuMgO_potentials_permuted_for_plotting.npz); channels 1-9 below use it, channel 0 (scalar, unambiguous) is untouched.

In [5]:
d = np.load("metawork54_results/AuMgO_potentials_permuted_for_plotting.npz")
mp = d["my_potentials_permuted"]   # torch port, e3x<->LOREM permutation applied to channels 1-9
jp = d["jax_potentials"].astype(np.float64)

fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 5, figsize=(15, 6))
for c in range(10):
    ax = axes.flat[c]
    lo, hi = min(jp[:, c].min(), mp[:, c].min()), max(jp[:, c].max(), mp[:, c].max())
    ax.plot([lo, hi], [lo, hi], color="0.6", linestyle="--", linewidth=1)
    ax.scatter(jp[:, c], mp[:, c], s=6, color=BLUE, alpha=0.6)
    corr = np.corrcoef(jp[:, c], mp[:, c])[0, 1]
    ax.set_title(f"channel {c} (r={corr:.2f})", fontsize=9)
    ax.tick_params(labelsize=7)
fig.suptitle(
    "AuMgO Ewald-potential channels: torch-port (permuted) vs jax reference (110 atoms)",
    y=1.03,
)
fig.tight_layout()

The four dominant channels (0, 1, 4, 9 -- the largest-magnitude scalar and l=1 components) now correlate at r=0.89-0.99: the charge/spherical-feature machinery upstream of the Ewald evaluation is fine. The six small-magnitude channels (2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8 -- l=2 quadrupole-scale components, std ~0.03-0.99 vs. ~2-7 for the dominant ones) correlate far more weakly (r=0.26-0.47) -- consistent with metawork-54's conclusion that there's a real, still-open residual specifically in the Ewald potential evaluation (torch-pme vs jax-pme), most visible where the signal itself is small relative to that residual. Every dominant channel's torch std is systematically ~1.3-1.5x smaller than jax's (e.g. channel 4: 2.18 vs 2.81; channel 9: 1.89 vs 2.77) -- not a single clean missing factor across all ten channels (the weak ones range 1.1-2.1x), but a consistent enough pattern in the strong ones to suggest a specific, findable numerical difference rather than noise.

7. UPDATE (after this notebook was first written): root cause found and fixed¶

The ~1.3-1.5x std-ratio pattern flagged just above turned out to be the whole story. metawork-54 ruled out a torch-pme/jax-pme numerics gap directly (a from-scratch NaCl rock-salt lattice with the exact, independently-known analytic Madelung energy -- both libraries reproduce it exactly, cubic and slab-like cells, neutral and non-neutral charges, with and without an exclusion radius), which meant the remaining gap had to be a wiring difference, not a library bug. Hooking the real lorem-jax forward pass directly (jax.debug.callback on Ewald()'s own potentials closure, not an external reconstruction) pointed straight at it:

JaxParityLongRange built its torchpme.CoulombPotential with exclusion_radius=neighbor_list_options.cutoff -- copied from the production LoremLongRangeFeaturizer (a different, intentionally-restructured port). lorem-jax's own Ewald() factory (jaxpme.batched_mixed.calculators) always uses exclusion_radius=None -- plain, unmodified Ewald, no short-range exclusion zone. That one wrong constructor argument was the entire source of the AuMgO/bio_dimers discrepancy. Fixed by removing it; also switched to marathon's actual smearing formula (smearing = cutoff/4, lr_wavelength = cutoff/8, derived from the checkpoint's own cutoff -- not a torchpme.tuning.ewald.tune_ewald guess).

Both energy and forces below are now at the float32 noise floor against the JAX reference -- not an improved approximation, essentially exact agreement. See metatrain's jax_parity.py module docstring and etc/lorem-parity/jax_checkpoint_parity/ in metawork for the full writeup.</cell_type>

5. Cumulene: warm-started fine-tune, training snapshot¶

Snapshot only -- cumulene_long_run_metrics.txt was copied while metawork-54's training run was still in progress (epoch 89 of a planned 200, append-only CSV so reading mid-run is safe). Re-copy the file and re-run this cell for an updated curve; this notebook will not update itself automatically.

Train loss is falling steadily (with periodic spikes, likely batch composition or an LR-schedule restart), but the sparse validation RMSE (every 10th epoch) is essentially flat around 5 eV / 60 eV/Å and not obviously improving over these 90 epochs -- worth metawork-54 keeping an eye on as the run continues.

In [8]:

6. bio_dimers smoke test -- diagnostic only, NOT a validated result (superseded, see section 9)¶

metawork-54 has no torch-side array for bio_dimers -- only jax-side energies/potentials generated while diagnosing a bug; the smoke-test's torch-side output was only printed to that session's own background task stdout, which isn't recoverable from here. This surfaced a real, still-open torch-pme vs jax-pme Ewald-potential discrepancy (the same family as section 4's AuMgO finding) -- treat the plots below as "what jax alone predicts", not a parity check.

Update: this was the same exclusion_radius bug as AuMgO's (section 7), now fixed. See section 9 below for the real, torch-side-included, validated comparison -- 200 frames, energy and forces, both checkpoint-loading fidelity (vs. JAX) and model accuracy (vs. DFT). Left as-is below for the historical record of what the bug looked like.</cell_type>

9. bio_dimers: full validated result (ran this myself, not a diagnostic anymore)¶

200 frames from bio_dimers_test.xyz (periodic, 30x30x30 Å box, Ewald), checkpoint evals/bio_dimers/lorem/run/checkpoints/R2_E+F, after the section 7 fix. Two different things are being measured:

  1. Checkpoint-loading fidelity (torch port vs. JAX reference) -- does the torch port reproduce the same checkpoint's predictions as running it in JAX? A weight-transfer/numerics check, nothing to do with model quality.
  2. Model accuracy vs. DFT -- how good is that checkpoint against the real DFT labels? This is the number the paper itself reports (0.222 meV/atom energy RMSE, 1.646 meV/Å forces, full 13,743-frame test set).

Data + reproduction commands: metawork's etc/lorem-parity/jax_checkpoint_parity/RESULTS_bio_dimers.md.

Takeaways (updated)¶

Original takeaways (sections 1-6, before the fix) are kept above for the record of the investigation -- how the bug was chased down is as useful as the fix itself. Current state:

  • SR (short-range) parity was always essentially exact for AuMgO (Dense_0 through Update_1, MLP_0/MLP_1: diffs at the float32 noise floor) -- same solid ground as the SN2 port (15_long_range_scan_lorem_jax_ported_torch.ipynb).

  • LR (long-range) parity is now also exact. The ~0.06-0.19 eV AuMgO energy gap and the much larger bio_dimers gap were the same single bug: JaxParityLongRange set exclusion_radius=neighbor_list_options.cutoff on its Ewald calculator, copied from a different (intentionally restructured) production class. lorem-jax's own Ewald() always uses exclusion_radius=None. Removing that one argument, and using marathon's real smearing formula (cutoff/4, cutoff/8) instead of a tune_ewald guess, fixed both periodic checkpoints:

    | | energy RMSE vs. JAX | forces RMSE vs. JAX | energy RMSE vs. DFT | forces RMSE vs. DFT | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | AuMgO, before | 0.71 meV/atom | 60 meV/Å | -- | -- | | AuMgO, after | 0.0002 meV/atom | 0.02 meV/Å | -- | -- | | bio_dimers, before | 26.9 meV/atom | 225 meV/Å | -- | -- | | bio_dimers, after | 0.0001 meV/atom | 0.003 meV/Å | 0.24 meV/atom (paper 0.22) | 1.73 meV/Å (paper 1.65) |

  • It was found by ruling out the library-numerics explanation with actual ground truth (an analytic NaCl Madelung-constant check, not just comparing the two packages to each other), then hooking the real lorem-jax forward pass directly to capture its true inputs/outputs -- comparing two black-box implementations against each other was inconclusive and initially misleading (see the "1.3-1.5x std ratio" note above, which turned out to be a symptom of the bug, not evidence for a numerics gap).

  • bio_dimers is now a real, validated result (section 9), not a diagnostic placeholder -- 200 frames, energy + forces, both checkpoint fidelity and model accuracy, matching the paper's own reported numbers.

  • Cumulene's warm-started fine-tune (non-PBC, uses direct_calculator rather than EwaldCalculator) got the same exclusion_radius fix but that run predates it and wasn't rerun -- expect it to do at least as well, plausibly better; not verified.

  • Bottom line, updated: the AuMgO/bio_dimers (periodic/Ewald) path of the ported torch model is now trustworthy to the same standard as the SN2 (non-PBC) port in notebook 15 -- float32-noise-floor agreement with the JAX reference, not an approximation.
